name: Squat
angleNote: Knee flexion: 0° = standing, about 100–110° = thighs parallel, 120° = deep. Lifting makes the angle smaller. Torques are per leg.

strength.note: Relative hip-extension torque vs hip flexion, assumed strongest with the hip bent. Peak is per leg, typical trained adult. Approximate.

strength.note: Relative knee-extension torque vs knee flexion, weakest near straight, strongest around 60°. Peak is per leg. Approximate.

strength.note: Relative plantarflexion torque, strongest with the calf stretched. Peak is per leg. Approximate.

muscles.name: Quadriceps
muscles.note: Knee extensors: their share follows the knee torque.

muscles.name: Adductor magnus
muscles.note: Rear part extends the hip, more so when it is deeply bent.

muscles.name: Erector spinae
muscles.note: Holds the spine straight; their load grows with the hip torque from the upper body. Approximation: driven by the hip's effort.

muscles.name: Calves (soleus, gastrocnemius)
muscles.note: Plantarflexors: keep the shin from tipping forward.

phases.name: Top
phases.text: Nearly standing: all joint torques are small.

phases.name: Mid-range
phases.text: Hips travel back and the trunk leans forward to keep the bar over the mid-foot.

phases.name: Bottom
phases.text: Around and below parallel: the hips and knees have their largest moment arms. Whichever joint's effort peaks first is the sticking point.

variants.name: High-bar back squat
variants.notes: Bar on the upper traps. The solver leans the trunk until the centre of mass of body + bar is over the mid-foot. The shin's forward angle is set to a third of the knee angle.

variants.name: Low-bar back squat
variants.notes: Bar about 6 cm lower and further back, knees a little less forward. The trunk has to lean more to balance, which moves torque from the knees to the hips.

variants.name: Front squat
variants.notes: Bar in front of the neck: the trunk must stay upright to keep it over the mid-foot, so the knees take more of the work. Needs more ankle range.

variants.name: Goblet squat
variants.notes: Weight held in front of the chest acts as a counterweight, so the trunk can stay upright even at depth.
